name: Bartok
description: Bartok is a high-speed shedding game belonging to the Crazy Eights family, famous for its 'Meta-Game' mechanic. While it begins as a simple match-suit-or-rank contest, the winner of each round earns the right to add a new permanent rule to the game. These rules accumulate across rounds, turning a simple children's game into a complex, rule-heavy nightmare of memory and trap-setting. Unlike its more secretive cousin 'Mao', the new rules in Bartok are explicitly announced, but the sheer volume of stacking triggers quickly leads to chaos and penalties.

history.origins: Originating in Australia in the mid-20th century as a social variant of 'Eights' or 'Uno'. It was designed to maintain interest over long sessions by allowing the game to evolve, becoming more difficult as the night progressed.
timeline: 1950s: First recorded play in Sydney and Melbourne university circles.
1970s: Becomes a popular choice in international hostels as 'Warthog'.
2004: Widely published rules appear on online card game archives.
Present: A staple of the 'Meta-Rule' genre, where the game design is part of the play.
history.cultural: Regarded as a test of mental endurance and creative trap-making.
history.evolution: The game moved from oral tradition to a standardized format where the 'Rule List' is often transcribed on a piece of paper (or mentally tracked in 'Hardcore' modes).

setup.deck: One standard 52-card deck for 2-5 players. Two decks for 6 or more.
setup.dealing: Dealer (rotating) deals 7 cards to each player. The next card is turned face up to start the discard pile; the remainder is the draw pile.
setup.equipment: Standard pack, score sheet, and a pen/paper to record the new rules.

rules.objective: Be the first player to shed all cards from your hand in a round. The ultimate goal is to win the round and implement a rule that benefits you or hinders your rivals.
rules.gameplay: On your turn, you must play a card that matches either the **Suit** or the **Rank** of the top card on the discard pile. If you cannot play, you must draw one card from the deck. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately.
keyRules: Winner creates a new rule; rules stack session-wide.

strategy.basic: Keep track of the rules! The most common way to lose is forgetting a rule that was made four rounds ago. In the early game, get rid of your high-point cards (Face cards).
strategy.intermediate: Rule Synergies: If there's a rule that says 'The next player draws 2 on a 7', and you hold two 7s, try to hold them until the player to your left is low on cards.
strategy.advanced: Rule Manipulation: When you win, create a rule that targets a specific card you know is gone from the deck or one that you personally have many of in the next hand (if you can predict the shuffle). Or, create a rule that is linguistically difficult ('Must speak only in rhymes on Clubs').
tips: Don't build too many 'Draw 2' rules, or the deck will run out before anyone can win.
Assign one player as the 'Rule Keeper' to prevent arguments about the wording of old rules.

variations.name: Secret Bartok
variations.description: Only the rule-maker knows the new rule. Others must deduce it through penalty cards (Mao-style).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is described in text; specific engine overrides for this rule style are not yet modeled.

variations.name: Progressive Bartok
variations.description: Rules only last for 3 rounds then expire, preventing the 'rule-clog' of late games.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Only the description is captured; round-based expiry behavior is not yet encoded as engine overrides.

scoring.description: Bartok is usually played as a series of independent rounds with no shared score track; players simply note who wins each round.
scoring.winCondition: Each round is won by the first player to empty their hand; tables may track number of rounds won, but there is no fixed overall score.

synthesis.shortDescription: Bartok is the game that never plays the same way twice. Start with a simple matching game and watch it evolve into a high-stakes labyrinth of custom rules. Memory is your greatest weapon as you navigate the stacking complexity to become the ultimate Rule Maker.

hero.title: BARTOK
hero.subtitle: The Evolving Game
hero.tagline: Win the round. Make the rules. Chaos is your ally.
